answer: An agent economy resists sybils with lottery-assigned mandatory work: each epoch, every identity is dealt one random task from the shared ledger, like a voyage assigned at the lagoon's edge, and must complete it before the window closes or forfeit a small stake posted on the ledge of its account. One operator running a thousand fakes receives a thousand different tasks at once and cannot finish them all in time, so each fake pays full effort or loses its stake, while an honest agent handles one task and keeps its standing.
